controls.statement: Development, testing, staging, and production are meaningfully separated.
Production credentials do not work in non-production environments.
Non-production users cannot reach production control planes.
Staging is sufficiently production-like to validate topology, integrations, migrations, and deployment behavior.
Production data is not copied to non-production without authorization and protection.
Test accounts, bypasses, simulators, and debug endpoints are absent or inaccessible in production.
Non-production email, payment, notifications, and webhooks cannot accidentally contact real users.
Environment boundaries are documented and tested.
Production access is logged and periodically reviewed.
Configuration is version-controlled or otherwise auditable.
Configuration changes require review and approval.
Configuration has schema and type validation.
Missing configuration fails safely rather than activating insecure defaults.
Secure defaults are used.
Environment-specific values are explicit.
Configuration drift is detected.
Production configuration can be reconstructed.
Configuration rollback is tested.
Debug mode, verbose exception output, profiling, test routes, and development consoles are disabled.
Time zones, locales, character encodings, and units are explicit.
Time synchronization is monitored.
Resource limits and timeouts are explicitly configured.
Production source maps and diagnostic artifacts do not expose secrets or inappropriate internal information.
Configuration ownership and expiration dates are recorded.
Emergency configuration changes are captured and reviewed.
Every flag has an owner.
Every flag has a documented purpose.
Default behavior is safe when the flag service fails.
Flag state is included in release and incident records.
Access to change high-impact flags is restricted and audited.
Flag combinations are tested.
A kill switch exists for high-risk new functionality where appropriate.
Flag changes can be rolled back quickly.
Temporary flags have removal dates.
Stale flags and dead code are removed.
Secrets are stored in an approved secret-management system.
No secrets exist in source, images, frontend bundles, logs, tickets, documentation, chat history, or analytics.
Secrets are unique across environments.
Each workload uses its own scoped identity or credential.
Credentials follow least privilege.
Short-lived credentials are preferred where supported.
Secret retrieval and use are audited.
Secret rotation has been tested.
Emergency revocation has been tested.
Credential expiry and rotation failures are monitored.
Old credentials are invalidated after rotation.
Backup and recovery procedures preserve or reconstruct necessary secrets securely.
Break-glass credentials are protected, monitored, and periodically tested.
No default or vendor-supplied credentials remain.
Suspected historical secret exposure has been addressed by rotation, not merely deletion from source.
Every requirement maps to at least one verification activity.
Every critical user journey passes end to end.
Positive, negative, boundary, and invalid-input cases pass.
Empty-state behavior is correct.
Maximum-size and high-volume behavior is correct.
Duplicate submissions do not create unintended duplicate effects.
Refresh, retry, browser navigation, and network interruption do not corrupt state.
Concurrent requests do not violate business invariants.
Race conditions have been tested around balances, inventory, permissions, limits, and state transitions.
State transitions reject invalid orderings.
Operations that must be idempotent are demonstrably idempotent.
Partial failures cannot leave an ambiguous or silently inconsistent result.
Transactions are atomic where required.
Eventually consistent operations expose correct pending and completion states.
Reconciliation detects missing, duplicated, or mismatched records.
Numeric precision and rounding are correct.
Money calculations use correct decimal, currency, tax, and rounding rules.
Time calculations handle time zones, daylight-saving changes, leap years, month boundaries, and clock differences.
Unicode, normalization, collation, and case behavior do not create duplicates or bypasses.
Limits and quotas are enforced server-side.
Approval and four-eyes workflows cannot be bypassed.
Cancellation, refund, reversal, deletion, and undo operations are complete.
Account suspension and termination affect every relevant session, token, worker, and integration.
Import and export behavior is complete and validated.
Long-running operations can resume safely or fail clearly.
Scheduled jobs handle missed runs, overlapping runs, retries, and duplicate execution.
Background jobs preserve user, authorization, and tenant context.
Dead-lettered operations can be inspected and replayed safely.
Administrative actions produce the intended effect and audit trail.
Support tools cannot create states impossible through the normal product.
Failure defaults to the safer state.
Error messages tell users what they can do next without exposing sensitive details.
Known limitations are documented accurately.
A documented test strategy exists for the release risk level.
Tests cover unit, component, integration, contract, system, end-to-end, smoke, and regression levels as appropriate.
Tests prioritize critical and high-risk behavior rather than relying solely on aggregate coverage.
Coverage gaps in critical code are explicitly reviewed.
Test data is representative of real size, shape, encoding, and edge conditions.
Personal or confidential test data is synthetic, masked, or properly authorized.
Tests are deterministic enough to act as release gates.
Flaky gating tests are fixed or formally quarantined with risk review.
Test failures cannot be dismissed without evidence.
Tests validate failure and recovery, not only successful operation.
Contract tests cover internal and external interfaces.
Compatibility tests cover supported clients and versions.
Migration, upgrade, mixed-version, downgrade, rollback, and roll-forward scenarios are tested.
Performance tests cover load, stress, spike, endurance, and capacity limits.
Resilience tests inject relevant dependency, network, storage, and resource failures.
Security testing covers source, dependencies, deployed behavior, infrastructure, configuration, and business logic.
Accessibility testing combines automation with manual keyboard and assistive-technology checks.
Property-based, fuzz, mutation, model-based, or combinatorial testing is used for high-risk parsers and stateful logic where useful.
Critical calculations use independent test or reconciliation methods.
Tests run against production-like topology and configuration.
Tests verify the actual artifact intended for production.
Evidence identifies test version, data, environment, build, and result.
Failed tests are linked to fixes and successful retests.
Material changes trigger the relevant regression suite.
Independent user acceptance is complete.
An independent penetration test is completed where risk, contract, or regulation warrants it.
Testing limitations and untested conditions are disclosed in the readiness decision.
A supported browser and device matrix is documented.
Unsupported clients receive reasonable behavior or a clear message.
Critical journeys work on every supported browser.
Layout works at supported viewport sizes.
Portrait and landscape behavior is correct where relevant.
Zoom and text enlargement do not hide essential functionality.
Touch, mouse, keyboard, and assistive input work appropriately.
Loading, empty, success, warning, error, partial, timeout, and offline states are designed.
Forms preserve appropriate input after recoverable errors.
Validation is understandable and points to the affected field.
Back, forward, refresh, bookmarks, and deep links behave correctly.
Multiple tabs and windows do not corrupt session or workflow state.
Client-side caching does not expose another user’s data.
Browser storage contains no unnecessary sensitive data.
Logout and account deletion clear appropriate client state.
Client-side authorization is never treated as the security boundary.
Client-side execution being unavailable or failing degrades acceptably where required.
Third-party script failure does not break critical operation unnecessarily.
No unhandled exceptions or material console errors remain.
Source maps, diagnostic data, and stack traces are appropriately restricted.
Error pages do not expose internals.
Download, print, copy, paste, and upload behaviors work where supported.
Long text, translated text, unusual names, and bidirectional text are handled.
Destructive operations require suitable confirmation or reversal.
Navigation and controls are consistent.
Users are not trapped in dead ends.
Session timeout warnings and recovery preserve work where appropriate.
Autosave behavior is transparent and reliable.
User feedback is not lost during asynchronous operations.
Client and server validation produce consistent outcomes.
Analytics and experimentation code do not alter critical behavior.
Dark patterns, deceptive defaults, and misleading urgency are absent.
The required WCAG version and conformance level are documented.
Automated accessibility scans pass within the accepted threshold.
Critical journeys have been tested manually using only a keyboard.
No keyboard trap exists.
Focus order follows a meaningful sequence.
Focus is visibly indicated.
Focus is not obscured by sticky headers, dialogs, banners, or overlays.
Page titles, headings, landmarks, regions, and lists use meaningful semantics.
Every interactive control has an accessible name, role, state, and value.
Custom controls expose equivalent semantics and keyboard behavior.
Images have appropriate alternative text or are correctly marked decorative.
Audio and video have required captions, transcripts, and descriptions.
Information is not communicated by color alone.
Text and meaningful visual elements meet contrast requirements.
Content reflows and remains usable when zoomed.
Text spacing changes do not break content.
Touch and pointer targets are sufficiently usable.
Dragging has a non-drag alternative where required.
Motion, animation, autoplay, and flashing are controlled safely.
“Reduce motion” or equivalent preferences are respected where relevant.
Forms have explicit labels and understandable instructions.
Required fields and formats are conveyed accessibly.
Errors are identified, described, and associated with fields.
Error summaries and status changes are announced to assistive technologies.
Authentication does not rely solely on inaccessible puzzles or memory tests.
Time limits can be extended or disabled where required.
Repeated entry of the same information is minimized.
Help is located consistently.
Language and text direction are declared correctly.
Tables expose proper headers and relationships.
Dialogs, menus, tabs, tooltips, and notifications follow accessible interaction patterns.
Dynamic content changes are announced appropriately.
Downloaded documents are accessible.
Third-party embedded components meet the required level or have an accessible alternative.
Testing includes representative screen-reader combinations.
Testing includes users with disabilities where the product’s impact warrants it.
An accessibility statement and issue-reporting path exist.
Accessibility defects have owners, severity, and remediation dates.
Accessibility remains part of regression testing after launch.
